# SavvyMe

> SavvyMe is a daily learning app: five minutes a day with a real, live 3D machine you can turn, open, break and fix,
> in step-by-step courses on how machines work, how things are made, electronics and AI. Lessons end with three quick
> checks, and daily, weekly and monthly streaks keep you going.

- Home: https://savvyme.amaete.com/
- Build your plan (a short quiz that picks your course): https://savvyme.amaete.com/start/
- The app (web, works on any phone): https://savvyme.amaete.com/app/

## How it works
- Pick a course. Each day unlocks the next lesson in order, grouped in weekly units.
- A lesson is a live 3D model with a short story, things to try, and three check questions.
- The first week of every course is free. SavvyMe Pro unlocks every course. No ads.

## Courses
### How machines work (47 days)
Open up your car, engines, dams, cranes and rockets while they run. By the end: Explain the engines, brakes, pumps and wings that move the modern world.
First week: Car engine (V8), Automatic transmission, Car brakes and ABS, The differential, Turbocharger, Electric car, Car airbag.

### Your car (21 days)
Open up the car in your driveway: engine, battery, gears, brakes, seatbelt and the clever little machines in between. By the end: Explain what every part under the hood does, and what is happening when something goes wrong.
First week: Car engine (V8), Spark plug and ignition coil, The fuel injector, Radiator and cooling system, The alternator, The starter motor, The 12-volt car battery.

### Machines at home (21 days)
The furnace, the water heater, the fridge and the faucet: open up the machines that run your home. By the end: Explain how the machines in your home work, and what to check when one stops.
First week: The furnace, The water heater, The smart thermostat, Split air conditioner, The LED bulb, The kitchen faucet, The toilet cistern.

### How things are made (35 days)
From crayons, chips and soda cans to the dishwasher, fridge and phone in your home. By the end: Explain how the everyday things around you are made, and how the machines at home work.
First week: Crayons, Pencils, Coins, Potato chips, Toy bricks, Toilet paper, Aluminum cans.

### Your body and the natural world (21 days)
Your heart, eyes and brain, plus bees, storms, volcanoes and the whole Earth, opened up while they work. By the end: Explain how your own body works and the natural forces around you.
First week: The human heart, The lungs, The eye, The inner ear, Neuron firing, The kidney, The digestive system.

### Electronics from zero (30 days)
Volts, LEDs, sensors and your first code on a board, wired by your own hand. By the end: Wire and program your own small gadgets.
First week: What electricity is, Volts, amps and ohms, How a breadboard works, Meet the board, Resistors and the colour code, LEDs, Buttons, switches and knobs.

### Smart home and gadgets (30 days)
Wi-Fi boards, phone alerts and dashboards for your home. By the end: Build sensors and alarms that talk to your phone.
First week: 3.3 V vs 5 V: meet the ESP32, Hello ESP32: your first web page from the board, Security light at dusk with motion, Doorbell that rings your phone, A clock that sets itself (internet time), Phone control over Bluetooth, Live sensor dashboard in the browser.

### Build smart gadgets (20 days)
Robots, gates, scales, ticket machines and trackers: real gadgets, wired and coded by you. By the end: Build moving machines and everyday gadgets for shops, streets and the road.
First week: Sweep a servo, Stepper precision: camera slider, Forward and reverse: H-bridge toy car, Line-following robot, Robotic arm: pick and place, Bean sorter by colour, Automatic driveway gate.

### Power, batteries and backup (14 days)
Measure batteries, watch the generator, ride out a blackout and run a solar grid. By the end: Build meters and controllers that keep the power on and the batteries healthy.
First week: Read a car battery voltage, Rechargeable lamp battery meter, Power is back! light-up alert, Generator fuel gauge, Generator hour counter for servicing, Generator fumes alarm (carbon monoxide), Voltage guard that cuts the fridge off on surges.

### Smart farm, garden and water (21 days)
Wire boards that water the garden, run the well pump, hatch chicks and warn of floods. By the end: Build sensors and timers that look after plants, animals and water by themselves.
First week: Soil moisture for a potted basil plant, Desert humidity and heat index, Drip irrigation timer, Tomato cold box with an evaporative fan, Solar dryer monitor, Bird scarer for a rice field, Smart farm: soil, weather, irrigation and SMS.

### AI, explained (30 days)
How machines learn, see and talk, and where they go wrong. No maths degree needed. By the end: Explain how a chatbot really works, and spot when it is making things up.
First week: What is machine learning?, Linear regression, Gradient descent, Logistic regression: the chance of rain, Decision trees: twenty questions for data, Model evaluation: how good is it really?, Bias and variance: too stiff, too floppy.

## About
SavvyMe has 11 courses and 273 hands-on lessons, and adds new ones every week.
